verdict.rationale: Codex docs describe sandboxed operation (isolated cloud environments, configurable permissions for editing files/running commands, and inspecting the 'active sandbox and writable roots') plus git checkpoints for reverting changes, which directly support sandboxed code/tool/network interaction [codex-docs-1, codex-docs-17, codex-docs-36, codex-docs-40]. However, a community report links to a GitHub issue asking whether Codex 'still reads sensitive data on your file system without even asking,' a concrete counter-example suggesting the sandbox/permission boundary can be bypassed or is weaker than documented [codex-comm-9]. Missing for 10: independent security audit of the sandbox, resolution status of the cited GitHub issue, and clearer documentation of network-isolation guarantees.
